fenced_json.notes:
Method: static read only. The review tools allowed no git or cargo runs, so I did not execute tests, clippy or the dry-run publish. The worktree's gitdir HEAD file reads 330986f574914ada17e79d074227527cce4eb9ba (matches the input commit). The branch name was not independently confirmed, because HEAD there is detached.

RULE-ADR-PLAN: the sprint doc's adrs list covers every binding repo-level ADR the sprint touches. There are no per-crate ADRs: docs/sc-jev-check/architecture.md holds no ADR sections. ADR-SAG-0025 and the four r-2b amendments are deliverables, and every listed id resolves to an Active ADR.

RULE-ADR-CODE: judge is called once per backend (run/mod.rs:568). Base validation happens before the first send (run/mod.rs:553). ChainContext requests are re-validated before their own send (run/mod.rs:659) and a refusal becomes a Failed backend with NotSent attestation and no log event. All-failed returns Err and leak is any Failed. A session-save failure keeps the answers and adds one warning with the code only. Digest recovery runs before send_with_busy_retry on the serialized body. It is attestation-only and never feeds the wire body. Its errors carry only a category and position (JevError::encode_failed) or fixed strings. There is no new disallowed_methods or allow(...) in the crates, no new ResolvedApiKey::as_str call, and test-util is non-default.

RULE-ADR-AWAIT-MUTEX: not applicable. The three owned crates (sc-jev, sc-jev-backends, sc-jev-check) contain no .await, and the Mutex uses in changed test files are synchronous.

Observations, not findings: the test-util WireFault public type family is recorded in the sprint doc and boundary notes but has no ADR of its own. It is feature-gated and covered by the ADR-SAG-0022 and ADR-SAG-0023 test-util convention, so I did not raise it. The ADR-SAG-0024 text ('RunConfig has no mode setter until r-2b') is time-qualified and still accurate.

findings.issue: Semantic question ids and choice labels are carried as raw String/Vec<String> (ParsedQuestion { id: String, choices: Vec<String> }). validate_questions re-parses the canonical bytes and re-runs the id-present, duplicate-id and choices-are-strings checks. wire::parse_answers (wire.rs:292-353) compares reply keys and labels as &str sets. backend::typed_answers (backend.rs:89-106) then validates each id a third time with QuestionId::try_from, after the paid judge call. PayloadBundle already holds the validated typed form (payload.rs:134, 235: question_choices(): BTreeMap<QuestionId, BTreeSet<ChoiceId>>).
findings.recommendation: Drop ParsedQuestion and the byte re-parse for ids and choices. Use request.payload().question_choices() (QuestionId/ChoiceId) in parse_answers and typed_answers, and keep only the 'type' and 'prompt' checks that the bundle does not cover. Id validity is then decided once, at PayloadBundle::encode. This also removes the case where an id passes pre-send validation and fails QuestionId::try_from as RESPONSE_INVALID after the call.
findings.evidence: validate.rs:14-17 and 110-150 build String ids. wire.rs:299-303 and 330-331 compare them as &str. backend.rs:97 calls QuestionId::try_from(id.as_str()) on reply ids that were just matched against those strings.

findings.issue: PreparedCheck.criteria is BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<String>>, so question ids and choice labels are raw strings. question_criteria, criteria_from_object and criteria_from_array (check.rs:245-329) re-validate and re-derive them from the payload bytes. parse_outcome (check.rs:226, 228) later converts them to QuestionId and ChoiceId via try_from and response_label. The typed map already exists on PayloadBundle::question_choices().
findings.recommendation: Build the expected-answer map from request.payload().question_choices() (QuestionId/ChoiceId) and have parse_outcome compare typed ids. Keep only the Jev-specific shape checks (object or array questions, at least 2 criteria) that the bundle does not cover.
findings.evidence: check.rs:22 and 245-329 build string maps. check.rs:226-232 and 240-243 re-validate through the newtypes.

findings.issue: default_backends() returns Result<BackendSet, JevError> for BackendSet::try_from(vec![BackendId::Jev]), a one-element list that cannot fail. The doc comment concedes this ('cannot fail'). The dead error path is propagated with ? from prepare (line 429) instead of being expressed in the type.
findings.recommendation: Add an infallible constructor on BackendSet (for example BackendSet::single(id) or Default) and return BackendSet directly. Otherwise make the invariant explicit with a single documented expect so the 'never fails' claim is auditable.

findings.issue: parse_count checks tokens >= 0 and then converts with u64::try_from(tokens).unwrap_or(0). The unwrap_or(0) fallback is unreachable and would silently turn an impossible conversion into a zero token count, which the later token-limit check would accept.
findings.recommendation: Use value.get("input_tokens").and_then(Value::as_u64), which rejects negatives and non-integers in one step with no dead fallback. This matches how nonneg() is handled elsewhere in the file.

findings.issue: criteria_from_object tests fields.is_none_or(..) and then calls fields.expect("checked above"). The expect is safe only because of the earlier branch (unwrap-safe by convention), and the same pattern recurs at line 200 (criteria.get(id).expect(..)).
findings.recommendation: Use let Some(fields) = fields.filter(|f| f.len() >= 2) with a single let-else early return, so no expect is needed.
